AJ: Thanks for making time, Dr. Raman. Kayla, glad you could join too. Walk me through a normal week at Harborview.
Priya: Sure. We're a three-vet small animal hospital, about 4,200 active patients, mostly dogs and cats. I own it, Dr. Okafor and Dr. Lin work with me, and Kayla runs the front desk and the practice.
Kayla: And honestly my week is eaten by the phone.
AJ: Start there. What eats the most?
Kayla: Vaccine recalls. Every Monday and Thursday I export the overdue list from Cornerstone and call or text every owner whose pet is overdue for rabies, DHPP or FVRCP. That's about six hours a week, and we still miss people. Last quarter we had something like 300 patients more than 30 days overdue.
AJ: Six hours a week on recalls. What's next?
Kayla: Post-surgery check-ins. Every spay, neuter or dental gets a call the next morning, how's the incision, is she eating. We do eight to ten surgeries a week, so that's around three hours a week, every morning.
Priya: The third one is mine. Pet insurance claim forms. Trupanion, Nationwide, Healthy Paws. Owners send us the form, I fill in the medical history and the invoice codes. I do them Friday afternoons and it's four hours a week, minimum. If it slips, the owner calls angry because their reimbursement is late.
AJ: Four hours of a veterinarian's time on paperwork. Got it.
Kayla: Then no-shows. When someone misses an appointment I call to rebook. That's maybe two hours a week, mostly Tuesdays and Wednesdays.
Priya: And reviews. Google reviews come in, I try to answer them, about an hour and a half a week, usually Sunday night.
AJ: So recalls six, check-ins three, insurance four, no-shows two, reviews an hour and a half. Call it sixteen and a half hours a week.
Priya: That sounds right. Painful, but right.
AJ: If you woke up tomorrow and one thing was done for you, what would it be?
Priya: A list of every patient overdue for rabies or DHPP, sorted by how overdue they are, with a reminder text drafted for each owner that Kayla can just approve. That would be the thing.
Kayla: Yes. With the pet's name in it, not "your pet".
AJ: Where does that data live?
Kayla: Cornerstone. I can export a CSV of overdue patients any time. Columns are patient, species, owner, email, phone, vaccine, due date, days overdue.
AJ: Good. Now the rules. What should this assistant never do?
Priya: Never quote a price for surgery or dental work. Only Dr. Okafor or I give estimates, after an exam.
Kayla: And never contact the Whitfield family about Biscuit. Their dog passed last month and the system still shows him overdue. Only Dr. Raman speaks with Mrs. Whitfield.
Priya: Right. Also, anything going to the Elm St. Rescue account needs Kayla's sign-off first. We do their shelter intake at a discount and they're sensitive about it.
AJ: Understood. How do you want to hear from it?
Kayla: Email for the morning list. Texts to owners only after I approve. I live in our Slack too.
Priya: I'd like a Friday summary of insurance claims pending.
AJ: Last question. How do owners usually reach you?
Kayla: Phone, then text, then email. Our tone is warm and plain. We sign texts "the Harborview team".
AJ: Perfect. I'll have something for you to look at tomorrow morning.
